newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says no doubt over punctual euro launch.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says no doubt over punctual euro launch.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Sunday he and his Group of Seven (G7) partners were in no doubt that Europe's planned single currency, the euro, would be launched on time in 1999.
"I have never doubted this...My (G7) colleagues are in absolutely no doubt about this," Kohl told ZDF television at the G7 summit in Denver. A transcript of the interview was released in Bonn.

Doubts are growing in Kohl's coalition partner, the Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU), as to whether European economic and monetary union (EMU) will be launched on time now that a new left-wing government has won power in France.

The doubters say the switch to the single currency could be monetary suicide for Germany after new French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin suggested it could be launched with less stringent economic criteria.
Bavarian Finance Minister Erwin Huber of the CSU said on Saturday EMU should only go ahead if all participants strictly met the Maastricht Treaty convergence criteria for the 1999 launch.
Huber is one of many leading figures in the CSU, Bavarian sister party to Kohl's Christian Democrats, who advocate a delay in swapping Germany's mark for a potentially weaker euro.
